description: Sync Intercom conversations and their replies, Intercom Tickets and published Help Center articles. Conversation and ticket access carries over from the assigned teammate and team when Enforce ACL is on.
opening: Sync Intercom conversations from the teams you select, or from the whole workspace, with every reply in them. Intercom Tickets and published Help Center articles sync for the whole workspace. Each conversation, ticket and article is one document. Each reply is its own document, linked to its conversation. The conversation document holds only the opening message.

A conversation and a ticket can be restricted to the assigned teammate and the members of the assigned team. Search applies this only when Enforce ACL is on. Internal notes are skipped unless you turn them on. File attachments are not synced, apart from text in pasted images.

permissions.who_can_read: A conversation, its replies and a ticket can be read by the assigned teammate and the members of the assigned team. These readers take precedence over the resource's. A team resource can be read by the team's members. The All conversations resource is open to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule on it. An unassigned conversation or ticket, and every article, follows its resource.
permissions.when_unreadable: If the readers of a conversation or ticket are incomplete or too many, it gets a permission warning, which you can find with `additional_metadata.rbac_warning`. Internal notes on an unassigned conversation get the warning too.
notes: Intercom does not report which teammates can see all conversations. A teammate who is neither the assignee nor in the assigned team cannot read the conversation in HydraDB, even when Intercom lets them see it.
Internal notes are synced only when `include_private_notes` is on.

connect.auth: Intercom uses an access token from a private app, or an OAuth access token.

credentials.name: access_token
credentials.text: An Intercom private-app or OAuth access token. An OAuth token reads only the conversations its teammate can see.

credentials.name: include_private_notes
credentials.text: Off by default. Turn it on to also sync internal teammate notes.

permissions.name: Read articles
permissions.text: optional. Without it, articles are skipped.

permissions.name: Read tickets
permissions.text: optional. Without it, or on a plan without Tickets, tickets are skipped.

steps.title: Create a token
steps.text: Create the token as a teammate with access to all conversations. If that teammate's access is later reduced, an OAuth token silently reads fewer conversations, so create a new token.

steps.title: Create the connector
steps.text: Paste the token as `access_token`. Turn on `include_private_notes` to also sync internal notes.

steps.title: Select teams or All conversations
steps.text: HydraDB lists your teams and an All conversations option. Select teams to sync the conversations assigned to them, or All conversations for every conversation the token can see. All conversations takes precedence over teams. Selecting every team still leaves out unassigned conversations.

connect.account: One connector reads one Intercom workspace.

sync.first_sync: Reaches back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default.
sync.changes: Each sync reads conversations, tickets and articles updated since the last sync. Every reply in a changed conversation is read again.
sync.edits: A changed conversation is read again with all its replies, and updates their documents.
sync.deletes: Conversations, tickets and articles deleted in Intercom can stay searchable in HydraDB.
notes: If Intercom refuses access to tickets or articles, they are skipped and the rest still syncs.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.rbac_warning
shared_attributes.text: Set on a conversation, reply or ticket when its readers could not be worked out, or on an internal note in an unassigned conversation. A warning does not by itself mean the item is public. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: acl
shared_attributes.text: The teammates who can read a conversation, reply or ticket, worked out as described under Permissions. Articles have none of their own. Not searchable.

documents.name: Conversations
documents.one_document: One conversation, holding its opening message.
documents.title: The conversation title, else the opening message's subject. Otherwise a title with the conversation id.
documents.text: The opening message converted from HTML to text, or the title when it is empty. The status, priority, tags, creation time and conversation id are part of the text too. The title is searchable too. Search the replies for the rest of the conversation.
documents.date: When the conversation was last updated, else when it was created.

attributes.name: status
attributes.text: Open, closed or snoozed, written as a `Status` line.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.text: `priority` or `not_priority`, written as a `Priority` line.

attributes.name: labels
attributes.text: The conversation's tag names, written as a `Labels` line, so a tag name in a query matches.

attributes.name: Conversation id
attributes.text: The Intercom conversation id, written into the text as the conversation's key. Keeps later syncs on the same document.

attributes.name: linked_ticket_id
attributes.text: Links the conversation to the Intercom Ticket it refers to. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.intercom_open
attributes.text: True while the conversation is open. Keeps only open conversations. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.intercom_read
attributes.text: True once the conversation has been read. Finds unread conversations. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the conversation was created, written as a `Created` line. Used as the result date only when there is no update time.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the conversation was last updated. Not searchable.

attributes.name: author
attributes.text: The opening message's author as `Name <email>`. The author is not attached to the conversation as a person.

attributes.name: tag_ids
attributes.text: The ids of the conversation's tags.

attributes.name: topics, topic_ids
attributes.text: The conversation's Fin AI topic names and their ids. They are not part of the searchable text.

documents.name: Replies
documents.one_document: One reply, or one internal note when `include_private_notes` is on. Parts that only record a state change, and redacted parts, are skipped.
documents.title: `Comment by` and the author. Without an author, the first 80 characters of the text.
documents.text: The reply converted from HTML to text, with its author, conversation id, and created and updated times. A reply that is only a pasted image is kept, and the text in the image is searchable.
documents.files: Text in images pasted into a reply is read and searchable. Other files are not synced.

attributes.name: author
attributes.text: The teammate or customer who wrote the reply, as `Name <email>`. The graph records the reply as written by that person.

attributes.name: mentions
attributes.text: Names @mentioned in an internal note. The names stay in the note text, and the graph records each as mentioned.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: The conversation the reply belongs to, written into the text as its id. Links the reply to its conversation.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.intercom_conversation_id
attributes.text: The id of the conversation the reply belongs to. Returns every reply in one conversation. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the reply was created, written as a `Created` line.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the reply was last updated, written as an `Updated` line. It is not the result date.

attributes.name: part_type
attributes.text: Whether the part is a reply, a note or another event with text.

documents.name: Tickets
documents.title: The ticket subject. Otherwise a title with the ticket id.
documents.text: The ticket description converted from HTML to text, or the subject when it is empty. Then a `Reporter` line. The creation time and the ticket id are part of the text too. The subject is searchable too.
documents.date: When the ticket was last updated, else when it was created.

attributes.name: reporter
attributes.text: The ticket's contact, written as the `Reporter` line, so tickets from one customer can be found. The graph records the ticket as reported by that person.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.intercom_ticket_id
attributes.text: The Intercom ticket id. Written into the text as the ticket's key. Targets one ticket, and keeps later syncs on the same document.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the ticket was created, written as a `Created` line. Used as the result date only when the update time is missing.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the ticket was last updated. Not searchable.

attributes.name: state
attributes.text: Open or closed. It is not part of the searchable text.

attributes.name: custom_attributes
attributes.text: The ticket attributes your workspace defines. They are not part of the searchable text.

documents.name: Articles
documents.one_document: One published Help Center article. Drafts are skipped.
documents.title: The article title. Otherwise a title with the article id.
documents.text: The article body converted from HTML to text, else its summary, else its title. Then `Author` and `Updated` lines. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the article was last updated, else when it was created.
documents.link_back: The article in your Help Center.

attributes.name: description
attributes.text: The summary under the title. Searchable when the article body is empty. Otherwise it is kept with the article.

attributes.name: author
attributes.text: The teammate who wrote the article, written as the `Author` line. The graph records the article as written by that person.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the article was last updated, written as the `Updated` line.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the article was created. Used as the result date only when the update time is missing. Not searchable.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: The collection or section the article sits in. Places the article under it in the graph. Collections are not documents of their own. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.intercom_article_id
attributes.text: The Intercom article id. Targets one article, and keeps later syncs on the same document. Not searchable.

attributes.name: collection
attributes.text: The Help Center collection name, or its id when the name cannot be found.

attributes.name: state
attributes.text: Always `published`.

example_searches: What did customers say about the checkout bug last week?
Which open conversations are tagged billing?
What does our Help Center say about resetting a password?

connections: A reply or internal note to its conversation.
A conversation to the Intercom Ticket it is linked to.
An article to its collection or section.
people: The author of each reply, and names @mentioned in internal notes.
The opening message's author and the assigned teammate are not attached to a conversation as people. Assignment decides who can read it.
graph.from_text: The opening message of each conversation, the text of every reply, ticket descriptions and article content.

not_synced: Internal teammate notes, unless `include_private_notes` is on.
Unassigned conversations, when you select teams instead of All conversations.
Contacts, companies and segments as documents of their own. Contacts only name people.
File attachments, apart from text in pasted images.
